sections.label: Key properties
items: Scale-invariant: magnitude is divided out, only direction (meaning) matters.
Guard against a zero-magnitude vector before dividing, or Python will raise `ZeroDivisionError`.

sections.label: Top-k + threshold pattern
items: 2. FILTER out anything below the minimum relevance threshold.
Filter before slicing: slicing first can wrongly exclude a high scorer that appeared late in an unsorted list.

sections.label: Why a threshold matters
items: Top-k alone always returns k results, even from an irrelevant collection, it has no concept of 'not good enough.'
'Best available' is not the same as 'actually relevant': a wrong-topic chunk sharing a keyword can still score moderately positive.

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Sorting or slicing before filtering by threshold.
Not guarding a zero-vector, letting `ZeroDivisionError` crash the whole retrieval call.
Assuming a non-zero score means relevant, without ever setting a threshold at all.

sections.label: Implementation checklist
checklist: Zero-vector inputs return score 0, never a raised exception.
Results are filtered by threshold before being sliced to k.
Ties/near-ties are broken by score, not by input list order.
